title: Find a failure without exposing private data
outcome: Produce controlled diagnostic events and an incident reproduction.
story: Amina reports that some requests fail. You need enough evidence to find the fault, but logging every message, password, or token creates another problem.

frames.explanation: A shared request id connects events without copying private message text.
Record what changed and prove the original failing operation now works.

sections.title: Observe outcomes and boundaries
paragraphs: Logs are records of events. Metrics summarize counts or distributions. A trace connects events from the same operation. Use a generated request id to connect frontend reports, server events, and provider outcomes.

Record safe event names, status, elapsed time, error code, and version. These can reveal where latency or failure occurs. A trace without private message content can still show that a provider timed out after retrieval succeeded.

sections.title: Use an allowed list of fields
paragraphs: Select fields to log instead of copying entire request or exception objects. Passwords, API keys, session tokens, customer text, and unrestricted tool output should not enter routine logs. Even ids can be personal data, so collect only what the investigation needs.

The lab returns a small allowed-field record. It is not a complete anonymizer: free-form request ids can themselves contain private text. The project generates ids on the service and uses a fixed event vocabulary, retention policy, and restricted access.

sections.title: Reproduce before repairing
paragraphs: Record the reported operation, expected result, actual result, version, and safe request id. Reproduce using disposable data. Narrow the boundary: interface, API validation, data query, retrieval, provider, or tool execution.

Make a focused repair and add a regression case for the original trigger. Do not clear errors by converting failures to success. Verify the main operation and inspect whether the repair changes other important outcomes.

sections.title: Recover and communicate clearly
paragraphs: An incident report states impact, timeline, cause supported by evidence, repair, verification, and prevention. If cause is uncertain, state what the evidence does and does not show.

A temporary fallback may keep the shop working while the model is unavailable. Distinguish recovery from permanent repair. Rehearse deletion and retention of logs, and verify that a secret sent in a test never appears in captured events.

words.meaning: Evidence about what a system is doing and where it fails.
A generated identifier connecting events from one operation.
A test that reproduces a previously fixed failure.

explanation: Only selected fields enter the output.
Status, duration, and code have explicit contracts.
The apiKey field is never copied.

exercise.title: An allowed-field diagnostic record
exercise.brief: Write safeLog(record). First select requestId and event; then add validated status/duration; finally add a bounded code and fixed event vocabulary. Extra private fields must disappear.

steps.title: Select fields explicitly
steps.task: Return only requestId and event. Missing values become missing and unknown.
steps.hint: Build a new object; do not spread the source record.

steps.title: Validate status and duration
steps.task: Add status from ok/failed/denied, else unknown. Add non-negative finite duration, else zero.
steps.hint: Check numeric values before logging them.

steps.title: Bound the vocabulary
steps.task: Use request/tool/provider events or unknown. Add code matching 1–40 uppercase letters/underscores or UNKNOWN. Limit requestId to 80 characters.
steps.hint: A fixed code is safer than an arbitrary exception message.

cases.label: Missing fields
cases.why: Missing input has a defined result.

cases.label: Negative elapsed time
cases.why: Invalid elapsed time is not recorded as real duration.

cases.label: Free-form error text
cases.why: Free text cannot become an event or error code.

project.title: A reproducible timeout incident
project.brief: Inject a provider timeout in the service workspace, follow its safe request trace, repair recovery behaviour, and add a regression test.

milestones.title: Instrument boundaries
actions: Generate the request id on the server.
Use fixed event and error codes.
Record duration and version without customer text.

milestones.title: Reproduce and repair
actions: Use a disposable failing provider adapter.
Locate the failing boundary from events.
Return an honest fallback and retain the user draft.

milestones.title: Verify and document
actions: Add the timeout as a regression.
Search captured logs for a planted test secret.
Write impact, supported cause, recovery, and prevention.

acceptance: Events connect using a server-generated id.
Private content and credentials are excluded.
The original failing operation has a regression.
Retention and access rules are documented.

tests.expected: A controlled fallback and diagnostic code.
The original flow succeeds without hiding errors.

project.extension: Add a latency dashboard and alert threshold, then test its behaviour with synthetic slow requests.
reflection: What data did you deliberately avoid collecting?
What separates recovery from the root-cause repair?
